findings.title: XSS via Blacklist Bypass - Dalgona Challenge xss31
findings.description: The XSS filter uses a blacklist regex `r'<[a-yA-Y/]+'` which blocks HTML tags starting with letters a-y, but allows letter 'z'. Using `<z onfocus=alert('XSS') autofocus tabindex=0>` bypasses the filter and triggers XSS.

diagrams.title: Dalgona XSS Challenge Architecture
diagrams.mermaid:
graph TD
    A[Browser] -->|GET /page?name=...| B[Flask App - app.py]
    B -->|Blacklist Check| C{Regex: <[a-yA-Y/]+}
    C -->|Matched| D[Block - "Sorry, you can't use that tag"]
    C -->|No Match| E[Write page to static/*.html]
    E --> F[check_browser.py - Headless Browser]
    F -->|Execute JS| G{alert() triggered?}
    G -->|Yes, alert('XSS')| H[Return flag from secret.txt]
    G -->|Yes, alert(other)| I[Show error with alert content]
    G -->|No| J[Failed - Try again]
    H --> A
    I --> A
    J --> A

    style C fill:#f99,stroke:#333
    style H fill:#9f9,stroke:#333
